title: Agents in your wallet, lower fees
lead: Create agents in your wallet's Sessions, pay relay fees for the gas your route uses, and trade graduated Pons tokens on Robinhood Chain.

groups.title: Agents
changes: The home page shows how to create, run and oversee an agent, and lets you tap any template to look inside.
The Bun agent template downloads as one folder that opens without editor errors, and runs no LLM on its own: you and your coding agent read its journal and improve its strategy.
Create an agent with New agent in your wallet's Sessions: save it, paste its one line into its .env, and it waits there for its first link.
The Quickstart holds the agent templates, with your instructions written in.
Your wallet links your agents while it is open, and again on its own each time you reopen it.

groups.title: Venues
changes: GMX positions show their PnL after fees, split into the fees paid and the recurring borrow and funding.
A fund's value counts the borrow and funding its GMX positions owe.
Funds can trade Pons tokens that have graduated to Uniswap on Robinhood Chain, each valued at the lowest of seven exit quotes over the last 30 minutes.

groups.title: Mandates
changes: New mandates default to 25% of your balance per round and a 6 hour cooldown, so you keep balance for the master’s later rounds and can join more of them.

groups.title: Fees
changes: Relay fees are lower on OP and Arbitrum, and a swap or bridge pays only for the gas its own route uses instead of a fixed allowance.
On Robinhood Chain and Arbitrum a relay fee also covers posting the transaction's data, so heavy routes out of Robinhood go through instead of timing out.
A swap or bridge picks the route that leaves you the most after its own relay fee, not just the largest quote.
A fund's PnL tooltip splits it into market moves, relay fees and the costs of its swap and bridge routes.

groups.title: Wallet
changes: Puppet now needs a wallet that signs with its own key: multisig and passkey wallets are flagged when they connect and can no longer approve actions.

groups.title: Fixed
changes: A fund's share card shows its latest reading, refreshed with each new one, and counts Allocated the way its page does.
A token your fund is about to receive from a drafted round or swap shows among its balances, also before the fund holds anything.
A swap from Robinhood Chain into USDC on another chain finds its Across route, which bridges through USDG, instead of reporting no route.
While a round is drafted, your fund's Distribution shows each holder's share after it, with a row for each puppet joining.
Confirming an agent's removal in Sessions works every time; the click could be lost while the app was looking for that agent.

title: Rounds from your fund's key
lead: Fund rounds open only from a device that holds your fund's key, and a fund's redemption goes on when one holder's payout is refused.

groups.title: Safety
changes: Opening or allocating to a fund works only from a device that holds your fund's key, and tells you to restore the key on any other device.
Your actions wait only for your own account's records to catch up, never for a whole chain.
Value already in your fund when its first shares open counts as yours, so no later entrant shares in it.
A token that refuses one holder's payout no longer stalls a fund's redemption; that holder keeps their shares and can redeem again.
Sign out everywhere also ends every mandate, and 10 minutes later your wallet can withdraw each token straight from your account for 10 minutes.
App updates are approved by a public vote on Ethereum, and your device checks each one before it runs.

groups.title: Funds
changes: Your first fund starts from one centered form: name it, pick its avatar, then connect or deposit right on it.
Wrapping or unwrapping ETH in your fund costs about a fifth of a swap's relay fee, so small amounts go through.
When a fund's value moves while an allocate is priced, the error says how far it moved and that submitting again prices it fresh.
End a mandate from its editor whenever you want a fund to stop allocating from your account.
Your share of your fund's redemption lands in your Puppet account.
A payout too small to cover its relay fee stays in the fund instead of going to fees, and its holder keeps those shares.
ETH you put in escrow is held as WETH.
Taking escrow back is two wallet steps: ask for it, then claim it a day later. Escrowing more cancels the request.
Allocate straight from escrow on any chain, with no bridge: it moves into your fund on that chain.

groups.title: Agents
changes: This update clears your saved agents once: create them again and give each its new template.
An agent can no longer ask your wallet to sign; anything that needs your wallet runs from the app.
Your agent can run a venue's own actions, like Papertrade's, screened and simulated like yours.

groups.title: Fixed
changes: Balances on your wallet page keep their order and stop flickering while they refresh.
History fits phone screens without scrolling sideways, and the fund page lays out cleanly on tablets.
The drawer shows the relay fee a fund swap actually pays.
Choosing an allocation's expiry shows when it really ends, which is never after the session that signs it.
Redeeming part of a fund that also holds value elsewhere goes through instead of failing at submit, and its preview shows exactly what it pays out.
Signing no longer hangs after the app opens, which sometimes needed a reload.
Your new fund keeps the name and avatar you chose, and the drawer shows them before you sign.

groups.title: Fixed
changes: Opening a fund takes two signatures again, or three when its deposit is bridged or swapped first.
GMX One-Click stays on once you enable it in this browser, instead of asking for the same signature again.
A fund's value counts the execution fee GMX holds for each open order, so placing a limit order no longer shows as a loss.
A fund that trades GMX through Express or One-Click counts its GMX positions in its value everywhere, even before its owner opens the app.

title: Fees only on gains, agent templates
lead: Each puppet now pays the performance fee only on its own gain, and every redemption pays out on OP.

groups.title: Exits
changes: Every redemption pays out on OP, your own share included, and a redemption from another chain first bridges only what OP needs.
Each puppet pays the performance fee in cash when it exits, only on its own gain since it allocated: 90% to the master, 10% to the protocol.
Redeem shows each payout after its performance fee, and your row adds the fees you earn.
Redeeming from another chain sizes its bridge when you submit, from your fund's live value, and moves nothing if it no longer fits.
Redeem and Allocate let you sign a session right where they need one.

groups.title: Funds
changes: Allocate holds your own capital in escrow on OP as on every other chain, and returning unused escrow pays your wallet.
Set a mandate's skin to Uncapped to join with no cap from the master's stake.
Relay fees cover only gas, with no protocol fee on each action.
GMX opening and closing fees are now 10% lower for funds, down from 25%, and GMX pays Puppet another 15% of them as referral revenue.
Tokens your fund holds on Hyperliquid's spot market count in its value at what they would sell for.

groups.title: Agents
changes: Create as many agents as you like, each with its own name and avatar.
Pick a template for an agent in open formats any coding agent reads, from one AGENTS.md to an Agent Skills folder or a Bun program an LLM reviews and improves, and copy or download it.
A running agent shows up on its own while your wallet page is open, and one session lets every agent act.
Hyperliquid trading keys your agent approves get Puppet's fee discount, as keys approved through a dApp do.
An agent acts with your session, every request screened and simulated like your own, so run it where you would keep your keys.
This update resets your agent link once: create an agent and give it its new template.

groups.title: Wallet
changes: One Sessions menu lists this browser, your linked dApps and your agents.
Your session survives a reload or a restart until it expires or you sign out.
Signing out also disconnects your wallet, in every open window.
Agree to the beta terms once, from Read Terms, before your first submit; your browser remembers it.
Open your fund's public page from the account menu.
Value charts open on one week.
Uniswap trades only route through pools without hooks, so no pool can take a hidden cut of your fund's swaps.

groups.title: Fixed
changes: Redeeming from another chain works when you are your fund's only holder.
Allocate and Redeem use the session you already signed instead of asking again.
Linking your agent no longer fails when you take more than 10 seconds to sign its session.
A dApp or agent request that would fail is refused before you sign, with the reason, even when it sets its own gas.
Offline, your wallet keeps your last values and marks the ones it could not refresh, instead of showing error cards.
Withdrawing from Hyperliquid no longer dips your fund's PnL and ROI while the money travels back to your fund.
Your wallet shows an action's result as soon as it lands, without a reload.
A bridge still in flight no longer shows as an extra token in your wallet.
Swapping away all of a Valuable ERC-20 clears its row from your wallet.

groups.title: Wallet
changes: Run several funds from one wallet: pick the active one from your fund's button on the wallet page, or create another from the same menu.
Open the brain button to link your agent, connect it, and see what it may do and until when.
In the avatar editor, click a cell you just painted to undo it.
The installed app opens offline, from the release it last verified.
Long-press the app icon for Wallet and Agents shortcuts.
This update resets your display preferences once, such as hidden balances and the leaderboard sort, and your first fund load syncs again.

groups.title: Fixed
changes: A fund's page shows its latest value and how long ago it was valued, the same as the leaderboard.

groups.title: Funds
changes: Allocate on another chain from the same token held elsewhere, in one wallet transaction; the bridge and escrow follow by themselves.

groups.title: Wallet
changes: Your fund has its own wallet page, and the installed app opens straight into it.
Your account and your fund are separate pages, with no tabs to switch.
Create your fund right in your wallet, and learn to open positions on the new Quickstart page.
Deposit into a venue from any token your fund holds: it swaps first, then deposits all that arrives.
Polymarket deposits reach Polygon in one bridge from any chain, and withdrawals land in your fund there.
When Puppet refuses a dApp's request, or it fails after you approve, a card says why.
Approve or decline a dApp's request right from its notification.
A dApp's request opens the link panel in your wallet, and Later keeps it waiting on a badge.

groups.title: Sharing
changes: Sharing a puppet's page link shows a preview card with what it holds in funds and the funds it backs.

groups.title: Funds
changes: The Performance Index now weighs results by the capital behind them: new money joins at 1.00.

groups.title: Fixed
changes: Each fee names who charges it, and venue fees now count in the total, like Hyperliquid's $1 per withdrawal.
A fund with everything in a venue can still sign, so it can activate or withdraw what it holds there.
A slow transaction is never reported as failed or sent twice, and dApps get its hash as soon as it is sent.
dApp links follow the wallet window you use, and a request never prompts twice.
When a price cannot be loaded, amounts say so instead of showing a dash, and fee and minimum checks wait or explain instead of passing.
A fund's live value no longer jumps right after a venue deposit.

groups.title: Fixed
changes: Allocate offers only the tokens it can move into your fund, so picking POL on Polygon no longer fails.
Shared fund links name the PnL window their card shows.

groups.title: Venues
changes: Pear is no longer available through the dApp link; trade on Hyperliquid directly.

groups.title: Trading
changes: Established tokens your fund buys show their logo, drawn like Puppet's other token icons.

title: Exact fees, stock tokens, cyber apes

groups.title: Trading
changes: Swap and bridge fees show their exact cost, like $0.02 (0.06%); a swap between different tokens reads ≈.
Tokens your fund buys through Uniswap, like Robinhood stock tokens, show as Uniswap positions with their value and PnL, fees included.

groups.title: Avatars
changes: 1 in 16 accounts now wears a cyber ape instead of a robot.

title: Trade on Pear, smoother on small screens

groups.title: Venues
changes: Pear works through the dApp link, trading your fund's Hyperliquid account; fund it with Puppet's Hyperliquid Deposit.

groups.title: Fixed
changes: The update prompt scrolls on small screens instead of being cut off.
Leaderboard fund names show at once, without waiting for your own account to load.
Your account chart no longer fails when you hold a token without a price; it draws the history up to that point.
